_comment: Hand-maintained, like errata.json. Not overwritten by tools/extract.py. Encodes the *order* of the procedures the booklet describes in prose (r202-r205, r215-r217) so `bp start`, `bp day` and `bp move` can walk them step by step instead of an LLM reassembling them from the text each turn. Every entry cites the section it comes from; nothing here restates game content that data/sections.json already holds.

setup.goal: Collect 500 gold pieces and return to the Northlands within 10 weeks (70 days). Day 71 is a loss, and so is the Prince's death.

steps.prompt: Read the opening. Stop before the caravan roll.
Roll 1d6 for wit & wiles. A result of 1 counts as 2.
steps.note: Replaying: if they won last time they may take wit & wiles one lower, if they lost, one higher.

steps.prompt: Roll 1d6 for starting gold: wealth code 2 on the Treasure Table.
Roll 1d6 for where the caravan dropped them.

standing: e002 is checked at the end of any day finishing north of the Tragoth River, after events but before the evening meal (e001, r215).

All six starting hexes are north of the Tragoth. e001's 'southern border' is the southern border of the Northlands Kingdom, which is the NORTH edge of the map - the Prince fled south and has not got clear yet. So expect e002 at the end of day 1 and every day until the party crosses the river southward. Getting south of the Tragoth is what the early game is about.
Ogon (0101) and Weshor (1501) add +1 to the e002 roll, and both are starting hexes - the guard looks hardest for you in the towns you might have run to.

actions.name: rest
actions.note: Heals one wound per character if no combat or escape happens. Still check for a travel event as if entering your own hex (r222), and rest improves hunting (r215).

actions.name: search cache
actions.note: Only for a cache you previously placed.

endofday.what: If the day ends north of the Tragoth River, check e002 now - after events, before the meal.
Feed the whole party. Mounts need fodder in terrain where the travel table says fodder is no.
Anyone who cannot be fed starves - resolve r216.
In a town, castle or temple, lodging must usually be bought.
Advance the time track one day. The game is lost on day 71.

day.one_action_note: One action per day, and the whole party does it. Some events grant a bonus action, others force the time track forward several days (r203).

move.lost_terrain_conflict: r205 says the lost check uses the terrain you are LEAVING; r205d says the post-river check uses the terrain of the new hex you are ENTERING. Both are quoted as printed - the specific rule is used for the river step and the general rule elsewhere. Travel events always use the terrain ENTERED (r204b).

speeds.foot: 1 hex per day if anyone is unmounted (r204a).
speeds.mounted: 1 or 2 hexes per day if everyone is mounted (r204a).
speeds.airborne: up to 3 hexes per day on winged mounts, flying all day, landing to camp (r204a). Winged parties may instead short-hop 1-2 hexes as normal mounted travel.

move.after_event: A travel event normally consumes the rest of the day (r204f). Exceptions: a fight where you killed everyone, and encounters that were only talk or negotiation - travel may continue if speed remains.
